image_description: A museum display featuring a fossilized Triceratops skeleton mounted in a walking pose. The skeleton is dark grey/black, set against a light beige sandy base and a background of museum exhibits including glass cases and informational signage. The skull features the characteristic three horns and large frill. The limbs are columnar with visible digit structures.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skeletal mount clearly displays two large supraorbital horns and one smaller nasal horn, matching the anatomical description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows a fossilized skeleton. The 'keratinous cutting edge' (beak) is soft tissue that does not preserve in fossils and is not present in this skeletal mount.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skeleton stands on four legs with thick, vertical limb bones consistent with weight-bearing columnar structures.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The large parietal-squamosal frill is clearly visible behind the skull, extending significantly wider than the facial portion of the skull.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears as a solid bony structure. While texture is rough due to fossilization/age, it lacks the fenestrations (holes) seen in other ceratopsians like Chasmosaurus.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a skeletal mount; skin, scales, and quills are soft tissues not preserved or displayed in this specimen.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The shoulder height is visibly lower than the hip height, creating the characteristic downward slope of the back towards the head.
The caudal vertebrae are visible and appear relatively short and robust compared to the body length, consistent with ceratopsian anatomy.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The distal ends of the left forelimb digits appear to merge into the ground/support structure without clear articulation or separation, looking slightly melted or fused.
The toes on the right hind foot lack distinct separation and definition, appearing somewhat blurred or fused together compared to the sharper left foot.
The text on the background sign ('...ceratops') is slightly warped and lacks the crisp geometric alignment expected from a camera lens, suggesting minor AI generation artifacts in background details.
